About 25 percent of the air is compressed in an air booster compressor. This boosted air is then cooled in an aftercooler against cooling water. The remaining five percent of the air is fed to a turbine-driven, single-stage, centrifugal booster compressor. This stream is cooled in a shell and tube aftercooler against cooling water before it is fed to the cold box. [58] All three air feeds are cooled in the cold box to cryogenic temperatures against returning product O and N streams in plate-and-fin HXs. The large air stream is fed directly to the first 2 2 distillation column to begin the separation process. The second largest air stream is liquefied against boiling liquid O before it is fed to the distillation columns. The third, smallest air stream 2 is fed to the cryogenic expander to produce refrigeration to sustain the cryogenic separation process. Inside the cold box the air is separated into O and N products. The O product is withdrawn 2 2 2 from the distillation columns as a liquid and is pressurized by a cryogenic pump. The pressurized liquid O is then vaporized against the high-pressure (HP) air feed before being 2 warmed to ambient temperature. The HP liquid O exits the cold box and is pumped to the 2 desired pressure before being heated to 27°C (80°F) and fed to the gasification unit. N is produced from the cold box at two pressure levels. Low-pressure (LP) N is split into two 2 2 streams, the first of which is used as the regeneration gas for the pre-purifiers before being recombined with the balance of the LP N prior to the compressor; the second LP N product 2 2 stream is used in the direct contact coolers chiller. HP N is also produced from the cold box and 2 is further compressed.
